body.statement:
For every \(L_{\mathrm{bd}}<U_{\mathrm{bd}}\) and every positive even \(n\), balanced complete randomization has the exact bounded-cube minimax value
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{bal}}[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]
 =\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}.
\]
Consequently, at the first three positive even sizes,
\[
 \mathfrak R_2^{\mathrm{bal}}=\frac{\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2}{4},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak R_4^{\mathrm{bal}}
 =\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2\left(1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right),
 \qquad
 \mathfrak R_6^{\mathrm{bal}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2s_6^2,
\]
where all risks have arguments \([L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]\).  At \(n=8\),
\[
 \Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2C_8
 \leq\mathfrak R_8^{\mathrm{bal}}[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]
 =\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}
 \leq\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2U_8.
\]
For every \(n\in\{2,4,6,8\}\), balanced complete randomization is strictly suboptimal in Hull's class of all bounded schedules and all measurable estimators:
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]
 <\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{bal}}[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}].
\]
For \(n\in\{2,4,6\}\), the certificate is
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{bal}}
 =\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}
 >\frac{\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2}{(\sqrt n+1)^2}
 \geq\mathfrak R_n^\star.
\]
At \(n=8\), the certificate is
\[
 \mathfrak R_8^{\mathrm{bal}}
 \geq\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2C_8
 >\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2I_8
 \geq\mathfrak R_8^\star.
\]
The independent-design endpoint action \(d_8\) has normalized worst-case risk exactly \(I_8\), attained only at Hull states \((k,\ell)=(0,3)\) and \((5,3)\).  The exact value of \(\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\), every comparison for even \(n\geq10\), Hull's uniform-in-\(n\) strict-suboptimality conjecture, and every asymptotic rate or constant remain open.
body.justification: A fixed-design tensor-product endpoint argument upgrades the endpoint-subclass lower bound to exact minimax-value equality, so the finite binary saddles now give exact bounded-cube balanced risks at two, four, and six and a two-sided bracket at eight.
body.gap: Hull's all-design theorem and numerical conjecture do not give these exact fixed-design values. The present result proves strict suboptimality only at four finite even sizes and leaves the exact eight-unit value and uniform conjecture open.
body.consumer: Users of \(\operatorname{complete\_ra}\) obtain exact worst-case bounded-outcome MSE values at two, four, and six and a certified bracket and strict independent-design comparison at eight.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(L_{\mathrm{bd}}<U_{\mathrm{bd}}\) and abbreviate \(\Delta=\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}=U_{\mathrm{bd}}-L_{\mathrm{bd}}>0\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\mbox{-}design\mbox{-}endpoint\mbox{-}reduction}\), specialized to the uniform law on \(\mathcal Z_n\), gives for every positive even \(n\)
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{bal}}[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]
 =\Delta^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}. \tag{11}
\]
This is a minimax-value equality obtained by a labeled-data multilinear extension, not a claim that the pair of success counts is sufficient for nonbinary schedules.

Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}n24\mbox{-}equality}\) gives
\[
 \rho_2^{\mathrm{CR}}=\frac14,
 \qquad
 \rho_4^{\mathrm{CR}}=1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}, \tag{12}
\]
and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}n6\mbox{-}seven\mbox{-}state\mbox{-}saddle}\) gives
\[
 \rho_6^{\mathrm{CR}}=s_6^2. \tag{13}
\]
Substitution of (12)--(13) into (11) proves the three exact bounded-class formulas in the statement.

We next compare these values with Hull's independent-design affine upper bound from Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}hull\mbox{-}independent\mbox{-}affine\mbox{-}upper}\).  At \(n=2\), \(\sqrt2>1\), and hence
\[
 \rho_2^{\mathrm{CR}}=\frac14>\frac1{(\sqrt2+1)^2}. \tag{14}
\]
At \(n=4\),
\[
 1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}>\frac19
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \sqrt3<\frac{16}{9}. \tag{15}
\]
Both sides of the last inequality are positive, and it follows by squaring because
\(
 3=243/81<256/81=(16/9)^2
\).  Since \((\sqrt4+1)^{-2}=1/9\), (15) is the required comparison.

At \(n=6\), the isolating interval in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}n6\mbox{-}algebraic\mbox{-}certificate}\) implies
\[
 s_6>\frac{29066256529188}{10^{14}}>\frac{29}{100}. \tag{16}
\]
Also \(\sqrt6>2449/1000\), since both sides are positive and
\[
 6>\frac{2449^2}{10^6}=\frac{5997601}{10^6}. \tag{17}
\]
Equations (16)--(17) give
\[
 s_6(\sqrt6+1)>
 \frac{29}{100}\frac{3449}{1000}
 =\frac{100021}{100000}>1.
\]
All quantities are positive, so squaring and dividing yields
\[
 \rho_6^{\mathrm{CR}}=s_6^2>\frac1{(\sqrt6+1)^2}. \tag{18}
\]
Combining (11), (14), (15), and (18) with
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]
 \leq\frac{\Delta^2}{(\sqrt n+1)^2}
\]
from Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}hull\mbox{-}independent\mbox{-}affine\mbox{-}upper}\) proves, for \(n\in\{2,4,6\}\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{bal}}
 =\Delta^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}
 >\frac{\Delta^2}{(\sqrt n+1)^2}
 \geq\mathfrak R_n^\star. \tag{19}
\]

It remains to give the rational independent-design certificate at \(n=8\).  For integers \(k,\ell\geq0\) with \(k+\ell\leq8\), define
\[
 H_{k,\ell}
 =\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}2^{-\ell}\binom\ell j
 \left(d_{8,k+j}-\frac{2k+\ell}{8}\right)^2. \tag{20}
\]
This is the normalized shifted-binomial risk in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}hull\mbox{-}bounded\mbox{-}global\mbox{-}reduction}\).  Every coordinate specified in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}n8\mbox{-}independent\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}certificate}\) lies in \([0,2]\), so \(d_8\) is feasible.  Put
\[
 D_0=2^{14}10^{12}=16384000000000000,
 \qquad \sigma_{k,\ell}=D_0(I_8-H_{k,\ell}). \tag{21}
\]
Substitution of the nine integer numerators of \(d_8\) into (20), followed by common-denominator arithmetic, gives the following exhaustive list.  Row \(k\) contains \(\sigma_{k,0},\ldots,\sigma_{k,8-k}\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
k&(\sigma_{k,0},\ldots,\sigma_{k,8-k})\\ \hline
0&(4577441792,3880130560,30789297309696,0,238862336,
53461707285504,105693419993088,97336380346880,3580346880)\\
1&(327965806819328,359818810488832,281843022690304,293958109724672,
358362791708672,371515404700672,283644940700672,97336380346880)\\
2&(660197382158336,530887778891776,581356140759040,631689073692672,
560408945692672,371515404700672,105693419993088)\\
3&(787093695625216,855369846626304,824582262626304,631689073692672,
358362791708672,53461707285504)\\
4&(985221165627392,855369846626304,581356140759040,293958109724672,
238862336)\\
5&(787093695625216,530887778891776,281843022690304,0)\\
6&(660197382158336,359818810488832,30789297309696)\\
7&(327965806819328,3880130560)\\
8&(4577441792).
\end{array} \tag{22}
\]
All entries in (22) are nonnegative, and the only zeros are at \((k,\ell)=(0,3)\) and \((5,3)\).  Because \(D_0>0\), (21)--(22) prove exactly that
\[
 \max_{\substack{k,\ell\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\\k+\ell\leq8}}H_{k,\ell}
 =I_8=\frac{481065022279}{8000000000000}, \tag{23}
\]
with precisely those two maximizers.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}hull\mbox{-}bounded\mbox{-}global\mbox{-}reduction}\) applies to the feasible action \(d_8\): its measurable Bernstein extension has separately convex risk on the bounded cube, and its endpoint maximum is (23).  Therefore
\[
 \mathfrak R_8^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]
 \leq\Delta^2 I_8. \tag{24}
\]

Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}n8\mbox{-}strict\mbox{-}separation}\) proves
\[
 C_8\leq\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\leq U_8. \tag{25}
\]
Multiplying (25) by \(\Delta^2>0\) and using (11) gives the stated two-sided bounded-class bracket.  Exact subtraction of the rational values gives
\[
 C_8-I_8
 =\frac{1489964546219114077997554988878251203581}
 {282893788917485944245799445288000000000000}>0. \tag{26}
\]
Combining (11), (24), (25), and (26) proves
\[
 \mathfrak R_8^{\mathrm{bal}}
 =\Delta^2\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}
 \geq\Delta^2 C_8
 >\Delta^2I_8
 \geq\mathfrak R_8^\star. \tag{27}
\]
Equations (19) and (27) prove strict suboptimality at exactly the four claimed even sizes.  Since (25) has distinct endpoints \(C_8<U_8\), it does not identify \(\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\).  None of the finite comparisons proves strictness for any even \(n\geq10\), a uniform statement, or an asymptotic rate or constant.
